entries.falsifiableTrigger: D2 falls sequentially for 2 consecutive quarters, or the vendor states it can serve all of the demand it sees.
entries.mechanism: Buyers order far more accelerators than the parts chain can build, so unserved orders pile up behind every shipment.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether memory and packaging output rises fast enough to close the gap between guided growth and customer forecasts.
entries.statement: Datacenter GPU demand continues to outrun NVIDIA's ability to serve it.
entries.title: NVDA demand durability

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Advanced-packaging waits fall below 26 weeks and stacked memory becomes available on demand for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Each finished accelerator needs both a packaging slot and stacked memory, so the scarcer of the two sets the shipment ceiling.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new packaging lines and memory plants opening on schedule.
entries.statement: Memory and advanced packaging are both capping how much merchant-GPU vendors can ship, with high-bandwidth memory sold out through 2027 and TSMC packaging booked out at 52 to 78 week lead times even as capacity climbs toward 130,000 wafers a month.
entries.title: Supply constraint binding

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The challenger's accelerator share fails to rise above 7 percent through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Working racks with named customers turn the challenger from a promise into a second place buyers can actually order from.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its rack volume ramp holds to schedule in 2027.
entries.statement: AMD's data-center sales nearly doubled to $6.7 billion in the second quarter of 2026 and its Helios racks are in production with Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Microsoft named, yet its accelerator share stays near 5 to 10 percent against NVIDIA at roughly 90 percent because volume shipments only ramp through 2027.
entries.title: AMD credible second source

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Merchant accelerator revenue growth exceeds custom-chip revenue growth for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Every workload a buyer moves onto its own chip is an accelerator order it does not place with a merchant vendor.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether custom parts keep their cost advantage once memory is priced in.
entries.statement: Hyperscaler custom silicon meaningfully displaces merchant-GPU demand growth.
entries.title: Custom ASIC substitution

entries.falsifiableTrigger: D6 for a current-generation part falls more than 20 percent within a quarter.
entries.mechanism: Scarce hardware and rising component costs let rental providers raise published hourly rates instead of discounting to fill fleets.

pendingChallenge.rationale: One provider is raising published hourly rates for a second time this year across every generation it lists, and it says booked demand now runs beyond two years.

entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how quickly new rack supply reaches the rental market.
entries.statement: Published accelerator rental rates are now rising outright rather than merely holding, with one provider lifting on-demand prices 17 to 21 percent from October and as much as 56 percent since May, while used-card asking prices sit below their earlier peaks.
entries.title: Pricing power persistence

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The vendor books China data-centre compute revenue above prior levels within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Policy removes a large block of buyers from the addressable market, so demand that exists cannot be sold to.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to licence policy changes on both sides of the border.
entries.statement: Export-control policy materially constrains addressable merchant-GPU demand.
entries.title: Export control exposure

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Vendor-financed accelerator commitments exceed 300,000 units within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: When the seller funds the buyer, reported demand partly reflects the seller's own balance sheet rather than independent budgets.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether third-party lenders take over the funding the vendor now provides.
entries.statement: NVIDIA still underwrites a large share of its own demand through site lease guarantees and outside investor money, having cut one customer guarantee from $250 billion to under $120 billion, capped a new site guarantee at $105 billion, signed platforms meant to raise over $500 billion from third parties, and now paused some deals under a compute-partnership programme carrying $36 billion of six-year commitments, which NVIDIA denies is halted.
entries.title: Vendor-financed demand circularity

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Every direct customer falls below 15 percent of total revenue for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: A handful of buyers place most of the orders, so one of them pausing removes a large slice of revenue at once.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the arrival of a broader tier of sovereign and enterprise buyers.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's data-center revenue is increasingly concentrated in a few direct customers, raising demand-durability risk if any single hyperscaler slows orders or shifts to in-house silicon.
entries.title: Customer concentration risk

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The vendor loses the number 1 revenue spot in data-centre Ethernet switching within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Owning the wiring standard means even competing chips arrive inside the leading vendor's system, which keeps the switching cost high.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to open wiring standards gaining named production customers.
entries.statement: NVIDIA now leads the data-center Ethernet switch market and sells that networking bundled with its GPUs, deepening a full-system moat that raises switching costs versus standalone accelerators and custom chips. NVIDIA took the top revenue spot in data-center Ethernet switching in Q1 2026 by pairing Spectrum-X and Quantum with Blackwell and GB300, and its NVLink systems cut cost per token, but no finding compares networking growth against compute growth, so the sharper claim that networking scales faster than compute is not supported.
entries.title: Networking attach as systems moat

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 2x improvement in cost per token over its predecessor within 1 product cycle.
entries.mechanism: Cheaper serving makes more applications worth running, so each price cut adds paying workloads rather than shrinking revenue.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether measured gains survive outside vendor benchmarks.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's each-generation drop in cost per token pulls more inference workloads onto its GPUs and widens the market it can serve.
entries.title: Cheaper inference pulls in demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Prepaid memory deposits fall below $22 billion or are refunded within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Non-cancellable memory contracts mean buyers have already paid for the parts that only make sense inside accelerators.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to any buyer walking away from a signed take-or-pay agreement.
entries.statement: Non-cancelable multi-year HBM contracts backed by billions in customer deposits lock a large share of future accelerator demand into place and reduce the chance that today's buildout is speculative.
entries.title: Prepaid HBM take-or-pay locks in accelerator demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The under-50 percent China cap is lifted or the current flagship is cleared for China within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Both governments hold a veto over the same shipment, so approvals on one side are cancelled by restrictions on the other.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a political trade settlement covering advanced chips.
entries.statement: China's reopening to NVIDIA is now blocked from both sides, with Washington allowing only case-by-case licences under a sub-50 percent cap and a 25 percent tariff while Beijing tells approved buyers to keep the licensed hardware in Hong Kong to protect its own chipmakers, so shipments stay trivial and no revenue has yet been booked.
entries.title: Conditional China re-opening with a capped ceiling

entries.falsifiableTrigger: AMD or non-NVIDIA designWins in production inference keep expanding for two consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Rival software stacks have improved enough that the largest buyers now run production work on non-NVIDIA chips, so software difficulty no longer holds them in place.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced gigawatt commitments actually run production traffic rather than staying pilots.
entries.statement: The difficulty of running existing AI software on non-Nvidia chips keeps customers on Nvidia even when rivals cut hardware prices.
entries.title: CUDA software lock-in sustains the moat

entries.falsifiableTrigger: S10 standard memory and flash contract prices fall for 2 consecutive quarters as new capacity opens.
entries.mechanism: Memory is a large share of each server's parts bill, so its price sets the cost of every new rack.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory plants reaching volume output.
entries.statement: Memory and flash prices keep raising what every AI server costs, with component waits of 32 to 40 weeks, memory prices up about 90 percent since late 2025 and contract prices up roughly 50 percent this year, and the leading vendor is now passing more than 15 percent of that increase into system prices from early next year rather than leaving it all on system builders' margins, while the largest contract builder still reports that high memory prices have not slowed customer spending.
entries.title: Rising memory costs inflate AI-server economics

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The challenger's rack-scale volume ramp slips beyond the second quarter of 2027, or a named vendor's second-half 2026 ramp moves into 2027.
entries.mechanism: Each vendor's ramp depends on its own packaging and memory slots, so their production dates do not line up.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to manufacturing delays at any single rack supplier.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's newest racks ramp into production from the third quarter of 2026 while AMD's rack-scale volume mostly arrives in 2027, so the multi-vendor supply wave lands in stages rather than all at once. Supply-chain reporting still has NVIDIA, AMD, AWS and Google parts entering mass production together and AMD's rack reached production with third-quarter shipments, but one account puts AMD's real volume ramp and first production output at the second quarter of 2027 because of manufacturing delays, and Meta's in-house parts only enter production in September.
entries.title: Multi-vendor accelerator supply wave in second-half 2026

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The largest 3 customers account for a falling share of data-centre revenue for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: A small number of very large commitments carry the growth, so one partner slipping moves the whole line.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether mid-size buyers start placing rack orders.
entries.statement: AMD's data-center accelerator growth depends on a small set of very large commitments, which concentrates both its upside and its downside in a handful of partners.
entries.title: AMD growth leans on a few mega-deals

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The part misses customer sampling in the second half of 2026 by more than 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Using standard memory instead of stacked memory frees the part from the queues that gate every other accelerator.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether customers accept lower memory bandwidth for inference.
entries.statement: Intel's Crescent Island inference GPU uses standard LPDDR5X memory instead of high-bandwidth memory to sidestep the advanced-packaging and memory bottleneck, opening an alternative supply route for inference chips.
entries.title: Memory-based inference chips route around the packaging bottleneck

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The foundry's gross margin falls for 2 consecutive quarters as capacity loosens.
entries.mechanism: Demand from accelerators, custom chips, networking and power parts competes for the same lines, so the foundry can price rather than discount.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to customers moving volume to rival packaging and foundry suppliers.
entries.statement: AI demand spreading across GPUs, custom ASICs, networking and power chips fills TSMC's capacity across nodes and lets it raise prices.
entries.title: Broadening AI demand tightens TSMC capacity and pricing

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A top cloud buyer cuts its 2027 capital spending guidance within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Spending rises ahead of the revenue meant to pay for it, so any disappointment forces order cuts.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether reported cloud revenue keeps pace with the spending plans.
entries.statement: Hyperscalers' sharp jump in AI capital spending risks a pullback if returns disappoint, which would cut accelerator orders.
entries.title: Hyperscaler AI spending may outrun near-term returns

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The vendor guides gross margin below 70 percent in a coming quarter.
entries.mechanism: Memory suppliers raise prices faster than the vendor raises system prices, so part of the margin moves upstream.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much of the memory increase the vendor can pass into system prices.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's gross margin is stepping down from 75% toward a stated floor of 71% to 72%, with 74% guided for the coming quarter, because memory costs are rising faster than the company expected, so the premium is now being partly given back to its suppliers.
entries.title: NVIDIA holds a premium gross margin as it ramps new chips

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The top 3 buyers' share of advanced-packaging output falls below 85 percent within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: A few buyers book nearly all the packaging slots, so any cancellation leaves capacity with no other bidder of that size.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to smaller designers winning their own packaging allocations.
entries.statement: A few AI chip buyers control most of TSMC's advanced-packaging output, so any one of them cutting orders would leave capacity that is hard to refill.
entries.title: AI packaging supply is concentrated in a few buyers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: rpoBacklog commitments turn shorter-dated so order-book duration shortens for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Buyers sign longer contracts to hold a place in the queue, which pushes the average life of order books out.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyers switching back to short-term purchasing once supply loosens.
entries.statement: Cloud and chip suppliers are signing longer-dated purchase commitments that push out the average life of their order books, so a growing share of AI compute demand is booked years in advance.
entries.title: Backlog duration lengthens as demand is booked years ahead

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A leading model provider reports flat or falling revenue for 2 consecutive quarters while raising compute commitments.
entries.mechanism: Rising subscription and interface revenue gives the labs cash flow that supports the compute contracts they sign.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether reported run rates convert into collected cash and narrowing losses.
entries.statement: Leading AI model providers are growing revenue fast enough that their heavy compute spending rests on real and rising sales rather than hope.
entries.title: Model-provider revenue scales to underpin the buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No Chinese domestic accelerator is used for a frontier training run for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Restrictions push local buyers onto local silicon, which grows volume even though the parts cost more.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic stacked-memory output, which caps how many local chips can be built.
entries.statement: China's home-grown accelerators now take gigawatt-scale inference orders, with one lab planning at least 160,000 domestic chips at a one-gigawatt site while keeping training on foreign hardware, yet their prices have risen 20 to 50 percent in about two months on memory scarcity, so the displacement is real but costly.
entries.title: China Domestic Accelerators Displace Banned NVIDIA GPUs

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The largest neocloud's net loss narrows for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Renting accelerators bought with borrowed money grows sales quickly while interest and depreciation eat the margin.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to rental price rises flowing through to reported profit.
entries.statement: Fast-growing neocloud GPU buyers such as CoreWeave are booking record revenue while their net losses widen.
entries.title: Neocloud GPU Buyers Grow Revenue but Deepen Losses

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A top cloud buyer sets a 2027 power target below its 2026 level within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Accelerators cannot earn until a site can feed and cool them, so electricity and buildings set the deployment rate.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to grid connection queues and permit timing.
entries.statement: Companies now size and cap their AI buildouts by gigawatts of available power, so electricity and site capacity increasingly limit how many accelerators they can actually deploy.
entries.title: Power capacity is becoming the binding limit on AI buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The two incumbents' combined share of custom design work falls below 90 percent within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: New entrants winning design work spread custom silicon across more suppliers, which lowers the concentration risk.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether new designers convert announcements into shipping volume.
entries.statement: Hyperscalers' shift to custom AI chips runs almost entirely through two outside design firms, so the alternative to merchant GPUs is itself concentrated in those two suppliers.
entries.title: The custom-AI-chip alternative depends on two design houses

entries.falsifiableTrigger: odmMonthlyAiRevenue at named contract server makers falls year over year for 2 consecutive months.
entries.mechanism: Contract builders only book revenue when hardware physically ships, so their monthly sales are a direct shipment check.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to parts shortages that hold finished racks in the factory.
entries.statement: Contract server makers post record monthly revenue as AI-server and networking orders ship in volume.
entries.title: ODM AI-server revenue confirms real shipments

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A neocloud's debt-to-equity ratio rises above 6 to 1 within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Fleets are bought with borrowed money against contracted cash flows, so the equity cushion under them stays thin.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit conditions and to contract cancellations by anchor tenants.
entries.statement: Neocloud operators fund their GPU fleets mostly with debt, leaving thin equity cushions.
entries.title: Neocloud GPU buyers carry heavy debt loads

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Co-packaged optics stays below 5 percent of data-centre optical modules through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Putting the optics inside the switch package ties cluster wiring to a new and narrow parts chain.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to optical engine yields and packaging capacity for them.
entries.statement: The move to co-packaged optics is reshaping how AI networking gear is built and supplied, tying cluster wiring to a fast-changing optics roadmap.
entries.title: Optical networking shifts to co-packaged optics as a supply lever

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A named United States plant slips its build milestone past 2027 within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: New American fabrication and packaging capacity adds a second place the same parts can be made.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to construction labour and equipment delivery inside the United States.
entries.statement: NVIDIA and its partners are committing to build AI hardware inside the United States at very large scale, adding fabrication and packaging capacity outside Taiwan.
entries.title: US onshoring broadens the AI hardware supply base

entries.falsifiableTrigger: rpoBacklog at named cloud providers fails to grow for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Contracts are signed faster than capacity is delivered, so the order book shows demand earlier than reported sales do.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the quality of the counterparties behind those bookings.
entries.statement: Cloud providers are booking compute contracts far faster than they can deliver them, so their reported backlogs now show demand better than their quarterly sales do.
entries.title: Cloud backlog conversion becomes the demand proof point

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A top cloud buyer returns to positive free cash flow while holding its 2027 capital plan for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Capital budgets now exceed operating cash, so the gap is filled with borrowing and share issuance.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to borrowing costs and lender appetite for compute assets.
entries.statement: The largest cloud buyers are turning to debt and share issuance to pay for AI capacity instead of funding it from cash generated by their businesses.
entries.title: Hyperscalers now borrow to fund the buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A new accelerator generation delivers less than a 1.5x efficiency gain over its predecessor.
entries.mechanism: More work for each megawatt lets buyers add output without adding power or packaging slots.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether vendor efficiency claims hold in production clusters.
entries.statement: Each new generation of AI racks does far more work per megawatt, which lets buyers add capacity even when power and packaging are capped.
entries.title: Efficiency gains stretch scarce power and packaging

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Stacked-memory waits shorten and suppliers report unsold capacity for 2 consecutive quarters before the end of 2027.
entries.mechanism: With almost no memory buffer left, any production upset feeds straight into accelerator builds.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to stockpile days rebuilding at the two largest suppliers.
entries.statement: Memory and advanced packaging now share the limit on accelerator shipments, with packaging allocation named the binding constraint on system availability while memory stockpiles at the two largest suppliers sit below ten days.
entries.title: Memory supply is the new choke point on accelerator shipments

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory supplier gross margins fall for 2 consecutive quarters as contract prices flatten.
entries.mechanism: Scarce parts price at what buyers will pay, so profit shifts from assemblers to the memory suppliers.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory capacity arriving and breaking the pricing grip.
entries.statement: Memory suppliers are earning extraordinary margins on AI parts, shifting profit from the server builders toward the memory makers.
entries.title: Memory makers capture a growing share of AI server profit

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new sovereign or enterprise cluster above 10,000 accelerators is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: States and large enterprises now buy full clusters directly, which adds demand that does not run through the big clouds.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to state budgets holding through political change.
entries.statement: National projects and large enterprises are now placing accelerator orders big enough to matter alongside the cloud giants.
entries.title: Sovereign and enterprise buyers become a new demand tier

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This supplier's data-centre revenue growth falls below 10 percent year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: A returning supplier with its own fabrication and packaging adds a third source of parts alongside the two leaders.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether its inference part wins named volume customers.
entries.statement: Intel's data-center and foundry businesses are growing again with better margins, adding a third source of AI-adjacent supply.
entries.title: Intel returns as a data-center supplier

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new vendor equity stake in a chip-buying customer appears for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Taking a stake in the buyer ties reported demand to money the supplier itself put in.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to competition authorities treating these stakes as tied selling.
entries.statement: Merchant accelerator vendors are now buying equity stakes in the AI firms that buy their chips, tying reported demand to vendor-funded customers beyond NVIDIA alone.
entries.title: chipmakers take equity in their own customers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: S10 standard memory spot prices fall for 2 consecutive months as suppliers restore capacity for non-accelerator parts.
entries.mechanism: Suppliers move wafers to the highest-priced memory, which starves the standard parts consumer products use.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much wafer capacity stays committed to stacked memory.
entries.statement: The stacked-memory shortage is spreading into standard memory and raising prices on consumer and general-purpose graphics parts.
entries.title: memory crunch spills into consumer and general-purpose parts

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new multi-year accelerator-to-memory supply agreement is announced for 2 consecutive quarters through 2027.
entries.mechanism: Buying memory directly moves the vendor ahead of other bidders for the scarcest part in the rack.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory suppliers preferring spot pricing over long contracts.
entries.statement: Accelerator makers are signing multi-year partnerships and joint development deals straight with memory suppliers to reserve future stacked-memory output.
entries.title: Chip vendors buy their memory supply directly

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The leading supplier's stacked-memory share falls below 50 percent within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Two rivals reaching similar yields and volume splits the supply, so no single maker decides who can build servers.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to yield performance at the second and third suppliers.
entries.statement: One supplier holds most of the stacked-memory market and the largest cloud buyers have locked up long-term contracts, so access to that single source now decides who can build AI servers.
entries.title: Stacked-memory supply sits with one dominant maker

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new diversion prosecution or approved-buyer list reduction is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Prosecutions raise the cost of physical diversion, which pushes restricted buyers toward renting offshore instead.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether authorities gain power to police offshore rental.
entries.statement: Prosecutions and shorter approved-buyer lists are closing the smuggling route into China, but renting banned hardware offshore remains an open channel that regulators have only just begun to investigate.
entries.title: Enforcement closes the gray route into China

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Advanced-packaging waits fall below 26 weeks while stacked-memory prices rise for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Packaging slots are added in large fixed steps while memory output can be tuned, so the tighter of the two keeps swapping.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to which of the two limits adds capacity first.
entries.statement: Advanced packaging is again the tighter of the two limits, with lines quoted at 52 to 78 weeks and allocation named the binding constraint on system availability, while memory makers add capacity and all three now ship the newest stacked parts in volume.
entries.title: Packaging tightness starts to ease while memory does not

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Flash contract prices for server drives fall for 2 consecutive quarters while the newest generation keeps deploying.
entries.mechanism: The newest racks add a large drive tier, so each system pulls far more flash than the last.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new flash capacity investment reaching output.
entries.statement: The newest accelerator generation adds a large storage tier that is pulling flash demand up sharply and is already showing up as rising server costs.
entries.title: Storage becomes the next scarce part in the AI rack

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Every major cloud provider publishes list rates for its newest rack-scale systems for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Scarce leading-edge systems are sold through negotiation, so public pages show only what is plentiful enough to list.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to newest-generation supply becoming plentiful enough to list.
entries.statement: Some cloud providers now quote their newest rack systems only through sales while others still publish rates for the same class of hardware, so public price pages show only part of what leading-edge capacity costs.
entries.title: The newest systems leave the public price list

entries.falsifiableTrigger: market-share-pct for the leading vendor stabilises or rises for 2 consecutive quarters while rival shipments grow.
entries.mechanism: Rivals are adding capacity faster than the leader can, so the leader grows while its slice of the total shrinks.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether custom chips keep their supply of memory and packaging.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's share of AI accelerators is falling even as its revenue sets records, so rivals are taking growth rather than taking business away.
entries.title: NVIDIA's share slips while its sales still grow

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A major buyer orders loose accelerators rather than vendor racks for a flagship cluster within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Performance now depends on the whole rack's wiring and cooling, so buyers compare assembled systems rather than chips.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to open rack standards letting buyers mix parts themselves.
entries.statement: Both merchant vendors now sell whole 72-accelerator racks with their own networking and software rather than individual chips, so buyers compare complete systems instead of parts.
entries.title: The rack, not the chip, is now the unit of competition

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Texas data-centre power additions exceed 5 gigawatts over the next 4 quarters as the pause lifts.
entries.mechanism: Sites wait on permits, hookups and construction rather than on chips, so civil work sets the schedule.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to permitting speed and construction labour availability.
entries.statement: New AI sites are held up mainly by land, power hookups, building shells and construction labour rather than by chip supply, with a Texas connection queue of roughly 474 gigawatts against only about 1.2 gigawatts of forecast additions and up to $8 billion of attributed lost data-centre revenue, while suppliers now name building availability, construction labour and equipment delivery as the pacing items and still report no transformer lead times.
entries.title: Grid equipment lead times gate new AI sites

entries.falsifiableTrigger: D6 for newest-generation rentals falls while prior-generation rates rise for 2 consecutive months.
entries.mechanism: General scarcity lifts rates on every generation at once, so the premium does not concentrate in the newest hardware alone.

pendingChallenge.rationale: One provider is raising published rates on every generation it lists, including its oldest parts, so the premium is not concentrating in the newest hardware.

entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how much new rack supply reaches rental fleets.
entries.statement: Rental prices for the newest systems are rising while quotes for the previous generation spread out and drift lower, so the price premium is concentrating in whatever just launched.
entries.title: The rental premium moves to the newest hardware

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Alternative packaging waits rise above 52 weeks, or no accelerator maker places packaging volume outside the leading foundry for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Shorter quoted waits elsewhere pull packaging volume away from the leading foundry.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields and capacity at the alternative packaging suppliers.
entries.statement: Accelerator makers are starting to route advanced-packaging work to Samsung, Amkor, ASE and Intel because those suppliers quote far shorter waits than TSMC.
entries.title: Packaging work starts to spread beyond TSMC

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The challenger's share of advanced-packaging output rises above 15 percent within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: One pool of packaging slots serves two product lines, so each processor packaged displaces an accelerator.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the challenger winning slots at alternative packaging houses.
entries.statement: AMD holds only about a tenth of TSMC's advanced-packaging output and must split it between its server processors and its accelerators, so every processor it packages costs it an accelerator.
entries.title: AMD's packaging slots force a product trade-off

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship ships with its originally planned 288 gigabyte memory configuration within 2 quarters of launch.
entries.mechanism: With a fixed memory pool, giving each accelerator less memory is how the vendor raises the number of units it can build.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to stacked-memory yields on the taller stacks.
entries.statement: NVIDIA is cutting the memory in its next top-end accelerator to 192 gigabytes, far below the one terabyte it previewed and below the 288 gigabytes of the current generation, because it cannot secure enough stacked memory and because sites cannot supply enough power.
entries.title: Memory shortage now shrinks the product, not just the volume

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The first Korean facility misses its 2027 target, or the letters of intent are not converted into signed contracts within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Memory supply, construction money and cloud demand sit in the same country, which makes it a natural second hub.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the announced intentions become signed orders.
entries.statement: NVIDIA and one Korean group have tied together data-centre construction, memory supply and cloud capacity in a partnership described as more than $500 billion, making Korea a second hub of the buildout alongside the United States.
entries.title: Korea becomes a second centre of the AI buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No accelerator or system vendor announces a shipping product using the high-bandwidth flash specification within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: A cheaper flash layer holds model data that would otherwise need scarce stacked memory.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether flash bandwidth is good enough for serving workloads.
entries.statement: The industry has published a first standard for a high-bandwidth flash tier and is designing racks around large drive pools, creating a cheaper memory layer that does not compete for scarce stacked-memory supply.
entries.title: Flash steps in where stacked memory runs out

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Two consecutive software releases deliver less than a 1.5x measured inference gain over the prior release.
entries.mechanism: Software improvements raise the output of hardware already installed, so competitiveness rises before new racks ship.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to independent confirmation of the claimed gains.
entries.statement: AMD is reporting large software-driven speedups on its current accelerators, which lifts its competitiveness now even though its new racks do not ship in volume until 2027.
entries.title: AMD's software gains arrive ahead of its volume

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This buyer's nameplate compute fails to exceed 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026, or its quarterly compute capital spending falls below $10 billion for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: One private buyer with its own capital and power is now ordering at the scale of a large cloud.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to this buyer's ability to keep funding purchases from its own cash.
entries.statement: SpaceX has built its compute fleet from 400 megawatts to 1.4 gigawatts in a year, spent $15.8 billion on AI infrastructure in a single quarter, and says it will build exclusively on NVIDIA while expecting a very significant share of NVIDIA's 2027 output.
entries.title: A rocket company becomes a top-tier accelerator buyer

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This supplier's share of 2.5D packaging capacity fails to rise above 20 percent within 4 quarters, or its bridge packaging misses 2027 mass production.
entries.mechanism: A sole supplier of one small input caps how much the alternative route can actually deliver.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to a second capacitor supplier qualifying.
entries.statement: Intel's bridge packaging is winning volume orders, but a single supplier of its silicon capacitors is already fully booked and the technology is described as a better fit for custom chips than for high-bandwidth accelerators.
entries.title: The alternative packaging route has its own choke point

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This designer's share of accelerators fails to exceed 5 percent within 4 quarters, or its first chip misses fourth-quarter 2026 production.
entries.mechanism: Money and a fabric licence from the market leader give a third designer a credible route into custom chip work.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether named cloud customers move volume to this designer.
entries.statement: MediaTek has raised its accelerator share target to 15-20% and puts its first chip into production in the fourth quarter of 2026, adding a third supplier to a custom-chip design market that two firms had to themselves.
entries.title: A third designer enters the custom AI chip business

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Used prior-generation server prices fall more than 40 percent within 2 quarters, or published prior-generation on-demand rates drop below $2.00 an accelerator-hour.
entries.mechanism: When new systems are scarce and dear, older hardware keeps earning because it is available and much cheaper.

pendingChallenge.rationale: Published hourly rates for two prior generations are being raised rather than cut, while retail pages still show those cards out of stock with no price.

entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast newest-generation supply reaches the rental market.
entries.statement: Prior-generation accelerators keep earning their place at about $6.16 an accelerator-hour on a published rate card, well above the earlier community and secure tiers, while retail pages show current merchant cards out of stock with no price at all.
entries.title: Prior-generation systems stay in service on price

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Wafer suppliers report spare 300 millimetre capacity or falling wafer prices for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Every extra memory plant needs the same blank wafers, so the squeeze moves one step further upstream.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to wafer capacity additions arriving before the new memory fabs do.
entries.statement: Silicon wafer makers are running their lines at full utilisation, prices are rising and buyers are signing decade-long deals, so the squeeze now reaches one step further back than memory itself.
entries.title: Silicon wafer supply tightens behind the memory crunch

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Reported remaining obligations stay below $1 billion for 2 consecutive quarters while new gigawatt commitments keep being announced.
entries.mechanism: Announcements state intent while accounting obligations state firm orders, and the two are still far apart.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether intent converts into disclosed contracted obligations.
entries.statement: AMD has announced multi-gigawatt customer commitments while reporting only $222 million of contracted obligations beyond one year, so most of its pipeline is still intent rather than firm order.
entries.title: AMD's announced gigawatt deals are not yet booked orders

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No hardwired inference product reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Fixing a finished model into silicon cuts the cost of serving it, which threatens general-purpose parts in cheap inference.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how fast models change, since hardwired parts age with them.
entries.statement: Accelerator vendors are buying startups that burn model weights straight into silicon, a cheaper approach to running finished models that could take work away from general-purpose accelerators.
entries.title: Hardwired inference chips emerge as a new rival to general accelerators

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Non-cloud owners sign no new rental or lease agreements for 2 consecutive quarters, or the rented share of their fleets falls below 50 percent.
entries.mechanism: Owners that bought more capacity than they use sell the surplus, which adds a middle layer of supply.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to these owners' own workloads absorbing their fleets.
entries.statement: Companies that bought accelerators for their own use are now renting much of that capacity to others, adding a new layer of supply between the chip vendors and end users.
entries.title: Compute owners outside the big clouds start renting capacity out

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Reported HBM4 yields fall back below 70% or contract prices keep rising for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Better yield only helps if wafer capacity is available, and stacked memory consumes three to four times the wafers of standard memory, so higher yields have not translated into more delivered supply.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to wafer allocation rather than yield, since wafer supply is now the limiting factor.
entries.statement: Both large Korean memory makers have pushed yields on the newest stacked memory to about 80 percent, months ahead of plan, which points to more supply reaching accelerator makers than today's sold-out order books imply.
entries.title: Memory yields improve fast enough to promise relief

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No compute-financing platform closes a funded transaction within 2 quarters, or the memorandums lapse without binding agreements.
entries.mechanism: Third-party capital now funds accelerator purchases that vendors and clouds used to carry themselves.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to credit markets repricing compute assets.
entries.statement: Large asset managers and banks are being lined up to finance accelerator purchases, moving part of the buildout's funding from chip vendors and cloud balance sheets onto third-party capital.
entries.title: Outside investors start funding the compute buildout

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This foundry's utilisation loosens or it reverses the 10 to 15 percent price increase within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: When the leading foundry is full, overflow orders fill the second one and let it price up.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the leading foundry adding capacity and taking overflow back.
entries.statement: Samsung's contract chipmaking business is now full enough that it raised prices 10 to 15 percent on new orders and cannot meet all the orders it receives, so AI demand is tightening capacity beyond the market leader.
entries.title: The second-largest foundry fills up and raises prices

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No customer shipments of the new system are reported within 2 quarters, or no named customer expands beyond its first system within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: A different silicon shape sidesteps the standard packaging queue while still plugging into existing clusters.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether first customers order repeat systems.
entries.statement: Cerebras is shipping a rack-scale system built from three whole-wafer processors with named cloud and research customers, and it plugs into rival vendors' racks rather than replacing them outright.
entries.title: Wafer-scale machines join the rack contest

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new vendor-guaranteed or vendor-funded site above 1 gigawatt is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Without powered sites its hardware cannot be installed, so the vendor funds the sites to protect its own shipments.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the vendor's willingness to keep site risk on its own books.
entries.statement: The leading accelerator vendor is now guaranteeing data-centre leases and investing in powered land so that sites exist for its own hardware to fill.
entries.title: Chip vendors start buying the land and power behind their customers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A large cloud buyer raises capital guidance and its shares rise on the day for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Investors mark down spending only when they doubt the return, so the reaction shifts with sentiment rather than with the budget itself.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to evidence that spending converts into reported profit.
entries.statement: Shares fall on the day a company raises its own capital spending whether it is a cloud buyer or a chip supplier, as when AMD's stock dropped more than 8% because its quarterly capital spending of $808 million came in well above the roughly $298 million expected.
entries.title: Investors now treat bigger AI budgets as a cost

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Capacitor waits for server grades fall below 20 weeks for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: A rack cannot ship without its cheapest parts, so long waits on capacitors gate finished systems.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to capacitor makers adding high-specification lines.
entries.statement: Waits for the small high-specification capacitors that every AI server needs are stretching toward 40 weeks, so shortages now reach parts that cost pennies as well as the expensive chips.
entries.title: Passive parts join the AI server shortage list

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new trading-firm compute commitment above $1 billion is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Trading firms buy compute for their own models, which adds a buyer group outside the clouds and labs.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to trading profits that fund these commitments.
entries.statement: Financial trading firms are now signing multi-billion-dollar capacity deals with specialist compute providers, adding a buyer group that sits outside both the cloud giants and the model builders.
entries.title: Trading firms become a new class of accelerator renter

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The next flagship launches in a single memory configuration, or the number of assessed memory specifications falls below 2 within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Scarce memory and limited site power force the vendor to offer several configurations instead of one.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory availability settling on one qualified stack.
entries.statement: NVIDIA is preparing its next flagship in several memory and power versions at once rather than one configuration, so scarcity is splitting a single product into a family.
entries.title: One flagship becomes several part numbers under scarcity

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A major vendor's next flagship arrives more than 24 months after its predecessor, or a named 2027 or 2028 roadmap part slips by 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Competition for scarce capacity rewards whoever ships the next generation first, so gaps between launches shrink.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging qualification timelines.
entries.statement: Accelerator vendors are compressing the gap between generations, so buyers face a new top-end system roughly every year instead of every two to three.
entries.title: Product cycles get shorter

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No model builder completes a custom accelerator design within 4 quarters, or an announced design effort is abandoned within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Labs with huge serving bills design their own parts to cut the cost of running finished models.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these labs can secure memory and packaging for their own parts.
entries.statement: The companies that build the largest models are moving from buying chips to designing them, adding a new source of custom silicon beyond the cloud giants.
entries.title: Model builders start designing their own chips

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The announced system price increase above 15 percent is withdrawn, or rack quotes fall for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Vendors protect margin by moving part costs into the price of the finished system.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to buyer budgets, which one supplier already says are limited.
entries.statement: The leading vendor is raising prices on AI server systems by more than 15% for shipments from early next year as memory costs climb.
entries.title: Chip vendors pass memory costs into system prices

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Mid-size cloud contract signings fall, or their capital spending drops below 20 percent of revenue, for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Labs that cannot get enough capacity from the giants sign long contracts with the next tier down.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to these providers' ability to finance the build behind the contract.
entries.statement: Smaller cloud providers are signing multi-year compute contracts worth hundreds of millions and spending a third of their revenue on capacity to serve them.
entries.title: Mid-size clouds win multi-year AI contracts

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Large United States cloud server procurement growth returns above 5 percent quarter over quarter with accelerator-led servers taking a rising share for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Agent-style work runs many small steps, which favours cheap general-purpose machines and storage over accelerator-dense racks.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether serving quality holds without accelerators.
entries.statement: Cloud providers are shifting part of their new server buying away from accelerator-heavy machines toward ordinary processors and storage as agent-style work spreads.
entries.title: Agent-style workloads tilt cloud buying toward general-purpose servers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Next-generation rack quotes settle below $4 million per unit, or quoted rack prices fall for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Prices per rack rise with content, but cheaper configurations and better output for each dollar break the simple doubling pattern.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory content per rack, which is the largest cost swing.
entries.statement: Buyers are being quoted about twice as much for the next generation of AI racks as for the current one, so the price of a unit of leading-edge capacity is rising sharply between generations.
entries.title: Each new rack generation lands at roughly twice the price of the last

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No named customer reports running two vendors' rack systems in one production cluster within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Scarcity forces buyers to take whatever parts they can get, so clusters end up mixing vendors by necessity.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to software maturity for splitting work across different chips.
entries.statement: Buyers are beginning to run machines from competing vendors side by side inside a single cluster, with each vendor's system designed to hand work to the others.
entries.title: Clusters start mixing hardware from rival vendors

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No hardware supplier raises new equity or debt above $1 billion for capacity or customer financing for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Capacity now costs more than these suppliers earn, so expansion is funded from capital markets.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to investor appetite for capacity spending that pays back slowly.
entries.statement: The companies selling AI hardware are themselves issuing shares and bonds to pay for the capacity they need, rather than funding it from what they earn.
entries.title: Chip suppliers now raise outside money to fund their own expansion

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The second design partner books no custom-silicon revenue from this buyer within 4 quarters, or the agreement lapses within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Second-sourcing the design work protects the buyer's chip programme from any single partner's schedule.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the second partner's parts reach production.
entries.statement: One of the biggest in-house chip programmes has added a second outside design partner alongside its incumbent, so even custom silicon now gets second-sourced.
entries.title: A large buyer adds a second designer for its own chips

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A named plant tied to public support is cancelled or delayed past 2028, or 2 consecutive quarters pass with no new government-backed capacity announcement.
entries.mechanism: State money removes the payback risk from very large plants, so public backing sets how fast supply grows.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to political change in the funding countries.
entries.statement: The largest new chip, memory and packaging plants are being announced with public support attached, so state backing now decides how fast supply grows.
entries.title: Government money underwrites the next wave of AI supply

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new chip supply agreement carrying customer warrants is disclosed for 2 consecutive quarters, or a disclosed warrant fails to vest against its first purchase milestone.
entries.mechanism: Paying partly in warrants preserves the buyer's cash and gives the supplier a stake in the buyer's share price.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to share prices, which set whether the warrants are worth anything.
entries.statement: Large customers are attaching share warrants tied to purchase milestones to their chip agreements, so suppliers take part of their reward in the buyer's stock rather than in cash.
entries.title: Big buyers now pay their chip suppliers in share warrants

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Mediation ends in a settlement with no strike vote within 2 quarters, or the rejected wage agreement is ratified within 1 quarter.
entries.mechanism: Memory output depends on a few plants, so a stoppage at one would remove supply that has no buffer behind it.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the outcome of mediation at the affected plants.
entries.statement: Union action at the memory makers has become a live risk to memory output, with a Taiwanese workforce moving toward a strike and a Korean union narrowly rejecting its wage deal.
entries.title: Labour disputes reach the memory suppliers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No tariff rule covering finished data-centre servers is published with a rate and start date within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Duties on finished machines would raise the landed cost of every imported rack, but only once a rule exists.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to trade policy decisions that have repeatedly slipped.
entries.statement: Washington is preparing semiconductor tariffs that would extend to finished data-centre servers, with duty-free import allowances sized to each company's US chip-fabrication investment, though no rate or start date has been set.
entries.title: Tariffs on finished AI hardware become a new policy risk

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The vendor discloses new commitments under the compute-partnership programme above $36 billion within 2 quarters, or a regulator opens a formal inquiry within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Credit support that steers who may rent the chips invites both partner objections and official questions.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how authorities treat conditions attached to vendor credit.
entries.statement: NVIDIA's compute-partnership financing programme has run into internal antitrust concerns and partner objections, and reporting says some deals have been paused, which NVIDIA denies.
entries.title: The vendor financing programme draws internal and partner pushback

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The vendor guides revenue growth within 10 percentage points of the growth implied by customer forecasts for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Guidance is set by what the parts chain can build, so the published number describes supply rather than demand.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory output, which the vendor names as the limiting input.
entries.statement: NVIDIA guided fiscal 2028 revenue growth to about 70 percent while saying customer forecasts implied roughly 140 percent, so its published guidance now shows how much demand the supply chain cannot serve rather than how much buyers want.
entries.title: Vendor guidance now measures the shortfall, not the demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No model developer signs a new capacity agreement with a power or mining company within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Firms that already hold land and power connections can offer capacity sooner than a new build can be permitted.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these owners can finance the buildings and equipment.
entries.statement: Anthropic reports data-centre capacity limits and has signed capacity agreements with a mining company and a power infrastructure firm alongside about $250 million of initial chip orders with a startup, so companies that already hold power and sites are becoming a supply route for model developers.
entries.title: Model developers buy capacity from power-owning industrial firms

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Spot memory trades within 1.5 times contract price, or a supplier reports uncommitted capacity, for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Long contracts take future output off the market, leaving unsigned buyers to bid for a thin remainder.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new fabs adding output beyond what is already contracted.
entries.statement: Memory makers have sold most of their future output under long contracts running as far as 2031, leaving almost nothing for buyers without a signed agreement.
entries.title: Memory capacity is booked to the end of the decade

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This maker ships no commercial stacked memory to a domestic chip designer within 4 quarters, or its 2027 availability target slips by 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Domestic stacked memory is the missing piece for a home-grown accelerator, so local supply directly lifts local chip output.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to yields on its first commercial stacks.
entries.statement: A Chinese memory maker has begun small-batch production of stacked memory one generation behind the leaders, and local chip designers are already testing it for commercial parts.
entries.title: China starts building its own stacked memory

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Revenue per gigawatt fails to rise between generations, or falls below $25 billion, within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: With power as the scarce input, the vendor sells how much revenue each megawatt of site can carry rather than chip counts.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to system pricing, which sets the revenue inside a fixed power envelope.
entries.statement: The leading vendor now describes its opportunity as revenue for each gigawatt of data-centre power, which rises to about $40 billion with the newest platform from $25 billion with the last.
entries.title: The vendor now sells revenue per gigawatt, not chips

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No custom chip using the vendor's scale-up fabric reaches customer shipment within 4 quarters, or the partnership lapses within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: If rival chips only work well inside the leading vendor's wiring, competing silicon still sells the vendor's system.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to open fabric alternatives gaining production customers.
entries.statement: The leading accelerator vendor has invested $3.5 billion in a custom-chip designer that will build its chips onto the vendor's own connection fabric.
entries.title: The leading vendor pulls rival designers onto its own wiring

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The platform drops support for a rival accelerator, or a rival vendor's models are delisted, within 2 quarters of the deal closing.
entries.mechanism: Owning where models are published puts the vendor at the point where developers choose which hardware to target.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the promised neutrality is kept after closing.
entries.statement: The leading accelerator vendor has agreed to pay about $12.9 billion for the main platform where open models are published and downloaded, putting it in charge of the shelf on which every rival's software sits.
entries.title: The leading vendor buys the open-model shop window

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Quarterly AI orders at this maker fall below $2 billion, or its full-year growth outlook is cut, within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Audited orders at a listed hardware maker give an independent read on demand outside the cloud giants.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to parts supply, since orders only convert when systems ship.
entries.statement: A large enterprise hardware maker booked record AI orders of $3.1 billion in a single quarter and raised its full-year growth outlook, giving an audited read on accelerator demand outside the cloud giants.
entries.title: Enterprise hardware makers show the orders in their own books

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The service misses its first-quarter 2027 availability date, or no named customer is announced within 4 quarters of launch.
entries.mechanism: Operators that already hold power and floor space can sell finished compute at a higher margin than space alone.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the operator can secure accelerators for its own fleet.
entries.statement: A large colocation operator is launching a packaged inference service built on the leading vendor's reference designs, moving from renting floor space to selling finished compute.
entries.title: Colocation operators start selling inference as a product

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The foundry reports it can meet current chip demand, or drops construction labour and equipment delivery from its named constraints, for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Capacity additions are gated by builders and tool deliveries, so spending more money does not shorten the wait.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to equipment maker output and construction labour supply.
entries.statement: The largest foundry says it still cannot meet chip demand while building about 20 plants at once, with construction labour and equipment delivery named as the limits and its own tool demand running at roughly 1.9 times what it projected nine months earlier.
entries.title: Building the plants is now as slow as filling them

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The commitment is not scaled beyond its initial $3.5 billion within 4 quarters, or the second-half 2027 delivery slips by 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Training robot control models needs cluster-scale compute, which puts machine makers in the same queue as the labs.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to this buyer's funding and to site delivery at its chosen location.
entries.statement: A humanoid robot company has signed an initial $3.5 billion compute commitment with stated intent to pass $6 billion and a deployment reaching up to 100,000 accelerators, adding a buyer group that is neither a cloud nor a model provider.
entries.title: Robot makers join the list of gigawatt-scale compute buyers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A named Chinese buyer moves frontier training onto domestic accelerators, or returns inference to foreign accelerators, within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Domestic parts are good enough for serving but not yet for frontier training, so workloads split by type rather than all at once.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic training software and memory bandwidth catching up.
entries.statement: Chinese buyers now keep training on whatever restricted foreign accelerators they can get while moving inference onto domestic chips, so displacement is happening one workload at a time rather than all at once.
entries.title: China splits training and inference across two chip sources

entries.falsifiableTrigger: A chip-backed loan is undersubscribed or repriced, or an operator writes down its accelerator collateral value, within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Lenders treat accelerators and their rental income as collateral, which unlocks far more debt than corporate credit alone.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to resale values for used accelerators.
entries.statement: Banks and private lenders are writing loans secured on accelerators and the cash they earn, so the chips have become collateral rather than just equipment.
entries.title: Lenders now accept the accelerators themselves as security

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Twelve-high or sixteen-high stacks become the main shipping configuration for the leading accelerator vendor within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Shorter stacks raise usable units per wafer, but improving yields remove the reason to give up capacity per part.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to stacking yields and heat behaviour in the taller parts.
entries.statement: Stacked-memory suppliers are shifting their main configuration for the leading accelerator vendor to eight-layer parts and cutting twelve-layer output, trading capacity per part for more usable units.
entries.title: Memory makers step back to shorter stacks to protect output

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new Indian site above 500 megawatts or accelerator order above 5,000 systems is announced for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Domestic demand plus cheap land and power is pulling gigawatt-scale projects into a third build region.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to local power delivery and to accelerator allocation reaching the region.
entries.statement: Indian buyers are committing billions of dollars to gigawatt-scale sites and placing binding orders for the newest systems, adding a third large build region alongside the United States and Korea.
entries.title: India becomes a new gigawatt-scale build site

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The named model developer's share of the designer's custom revenue fails to rise for 2 consecutive quarters, or its chip programme is dropped within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Labs have the largest serving bills, so custom silicon pays back for them faster than for anyone else.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to lab funding, since custom programmes need years of committed volume.
entries.statement: Custom-chip demand is shifting from the cloud giants to the model developers, with one lab expected to become the largest custom-chip customer of the leading designer next year.
entries.title: Model labs become the biggest custom-chip customers

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This buyer raises funding covering its signed commitments, or its total signed compute agreements stop growing, for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Commitments signed ahead of funding leave a gap that only future fundraising or contract cancellation can close.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to private capital markets staying open to this lab.
entries.statement: A single model lab has signed about $517 billion of compute agreements in eleven months against roughly $180 billion of rental spending it had guided investors toward through 2029, with the commitments resting on money it has not yet raised.
entries.title: One lab's compute promises outrun its own spending plan

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No Chinese accelerator ships with domestic stacked memory within 4 quarters, or the maker's 2027 availability target slips by 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Pairing local chips with local memory removes the last imported part from the domestic accelerator.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic memory yields and packaging capability.
entries.statement: Chinese buyers are pairing domestic accelerators with domestic stacked memory, with one lab planning at least 160,000 home-made chips at a one-gigawatt site while two local designers test a Chinese maker's stacked memory for commercial parts.
entries.title: China assembles a home-made stack from chip to memory

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This buyer's licence-free access is renewed without a change of ownership, or lapses, within 3 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Access is granted to owners rather than to machines, so who holds the shares decides which chips a buyer can run.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to how American authorities treat foreign ownership of compute buyers.
entries.statement: A large Gulf buyer's licence-free access to the newest accelerators lapses around April 2027 unless it moves its headquarters to the United States, and its executives have held exploratory talks about selling a controlling stake to American firms.
entries.title: Chip access now depends on who owns the buyer

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory stockpiles at the two largest suppliers rise back above 20 days for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: With no inventory cushion, any plant problem passes straight through to accelerator builds within weeks.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to labour or technical upsets at the two largest memory plants.
entries.statement: Memory stockpiles at the two largest suppliers have fallen below ten days of supply, so any production upset now feeds straight through to accelerator builds.
entries.title: Memory buffers have run down to almost nothing

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No new generation project above 1 gigawatt is announced for AI data centres for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Grid queues are too slow, so buyers fund dedicated generation next to the site instead of waiting.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to permitting and turbine delivery times.
entries.statement: New electricity generation is being funded and sited expressly to serve AI data centres rather than general demand.
entries.title: Power plants are now built specifically for AI sites

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The next frontier training run reported uses fewer accelerators than its predecessor, or no run above 100,000 accelerators is reported for 4 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Each frontier model needs more compute than the last, so one run now absorbs the output of whole factories.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to training methods that cut compute for the same model quality.
entries.statement: A single frontier training run now occupies more than 100,000 rack-scale systems, with several times that number being brought online for the next one.
entries.title: One training run now fills a hundred thousand systems

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The published committed rate rises above merchant on-demand pricing, or the price page is withdrawn, within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Publishing a rate turns an in-house chip into a priced alternative that buyers can compare directly with merchant rentals.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether the cloud keeps enough of its own chips free to rent out.
entries.statement: One cloud giant now publishes hourly list prices for its own AI chip, and its three-year committed rate undercuts what buyers pay to rent merchant accelerators.
entries.title: Cloud chips get a published rental price

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Data-centre royalty revenue growth falls below 10 percent year over year for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Every accelerator rack needs host processors, and agent-style serving adds ordinary-processor work of its own.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to processor supply, which is already named a brake on server shipments.
entries.statement: Data-centre royalties on general-purpose processor designs more than doubled in a year and a new finished data-centre part already has over $2 billion of demand, so the buildout is lifting ordinary processors as well as accelerators.
entries.title: General-purpose server processors ride the AI wave

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This venture reaches 500 megawatts on its 2027 target, or a further funded compute venture reports a site delay, within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Money arrives faster than permits, power and buildings, so funded ventures still slip on physical delivery.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to permitting timelines at each named site.
entries.statement: A compute venture backed by $5 billion of investor equity is already at risk of missing its 500 megawatt target for 2027 because of site delays.
entries.title: Investor-funded compute ventures hit site delays

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory's share of AI infrastructure spending falls below 40 percent, or memory contract prices fall, for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Memory prices rise faster than any other part, so it absorbs a growing share of each infrastructure dollar.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to new memory supply breaking the price trend.
entries.statement: Memory is set to absorb more than half of all AI infrastructure spending within a year, up from about a seventh two years earlier.
entries.title: Memory takes the biggest slice of the AI budget

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Domestic accelerator prices fall for 2 consecutive quarters, or a Chinese maker ships commercial stacked memory in volume within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Local chips still need stacked memory that controls block, so scarcity shows up as higher prices rather than fewer sales.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic stacked-memory production reaching commercial volume.
entries.statement: Chinese accelerator makers are raising prices because they cannot get enough stacked memory, so the home-grown alternative is getting more expensive rather than cheaper.
entries.title: China's memory shortage raises the price of its own chips

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This buyer's announced spending plan falls below $30 billion a year, or no further offshore facility above $5 billion is raised, within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Building offshore with borrowed foreign money lets a restricted buyer use silicon it cannot import at home.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to rules on restricted buyers renting or owning capacity abroad.
entries.statement: A large Chinese technology buyer has raised nearly $30 billion of syndicated debt on tighter terms to build AI capacity outside China using non-restricted silicon.
entries.title: Chinese buyers borrow abroad to build outside China

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Neither part reaches customer sampling within 4 quarters, or the announced 2027 production dates slip by 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: The gap the established suppliers cannot fill is large enough to fund new entrants aimed straight at it.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether these startups can secure their own packaging capacity.
entries.statement: Funded startups are building memory and inference silicon aimed squarely at the shortage the established suppliers cannot cover.
entries.title: New memory startups aim at the inference gap

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Memory contract prices keep rising for 2 consecutive quarters after the efficiency claim, or no further model release reports lower memory needs within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: If models need less memory for each answer, token growth stops pulling memory purchases with it.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether other labs report the same lower memory needs.
entries.statement: A leading model developer says its newest models need less high-bandwidth memory, and memory suppliers' shares fell on the news.
entries.title: Leaner models start to threaten the memory story

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No major cloud reports capacity-driven customer restrictions for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: When capacity runs out, providers ration access, so lost sales rather than price cuts become the visible symptom.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to the pace at which new capacity comes online.
entries.statement: Shortages of hardware have pushed one large cloud to refuse customers and restrict subscriptions while another says demand still exceeds what it can deliver.
entries.title: Cloud providers now turn paying customers away

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The investigation closes with no action within 4 quarters, or a second formal information request is issued within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Deals that buy capability without a merger filing invite review, which can slow or reshape how the vendor expands.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to whether authorities extend scrutiny to the platform purchase and financing deals.
entries.statement: A United States authority is examining whether the leading vendor structured a $17 billion licensing and hiring deal to avoid merger review, and has sent it a formal information request.
entries.title: Competition authorities start examining the leading vendor's deals

entries.falsifiableTrigger: This designer's AI semiconductor revenue fails to exceed $115 billion in fiscal 2027, or its growth slows for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Each new lab or cloud programme adds committed volume, so custom revenue compounds toward merchant scale.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory and packaging allocation for custom parts.
entries.statement: The largest custom chip designer expects its artificial-intelligence revenue to rise from about $58 billion this year to $115 billion in 2027 and $230 billion in 2028, a pace that would put purpose-built silicon on the same scale as merchant accelerators.
entries.title: Custom chip revenue compounds toward merchant scale

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Volume production of the 512 gigabyte module slips past the second half of 2027, or no server maker qualifies it within 4 quarters.
entries.mechanism: Denser modules add capacity per socket without needing more stacked memory or more slots.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to qualification results on production server platforms.
entries.statement: Memory makers are demonstrating far larger server modules that cut power and slot count, offering a way to add capacity without more stacked memory.
entries.title: Bigger memory modules become a way around the shortage

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The 8.4 gigawatt 2029 target is cut, or no further named order above 100 megawatts follows within 2 quarters.
entries.mechanism: A national budget behind accelerator purchases creates demand that does not depend on any company's return on investment.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to political continuity behind the programme.
entries.statement: Korea's government has committed $919 billion to build 8.4 gigawatts of data-centre computing by 2029 and 18.4 gigawatts by 2035, putting a national budget directly behind accelerator demand.
entries.title: A state budget now funds gigawatt-scale compute

entries.falsifiableTrigger: Long-term supply commitments fall back below $150 billion, or fail to grow, for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Paying years ahead reserves the scarcest part in the rack and pushes rival buyers further back in the queue.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory prices, which set what those commitments buy.
entries.statement: The leading accelerator vendor's long-term supply commitments jumped to $279 billion from $119 billion in three months, mostly to lock in memory for its newest platform.
entries.title: The leading vendor prepays years of memory supply

entries.falsifiableTrigger: The 9,800 exaflop 2030 target is cut, or domestic capacity fails to grow for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: A funded state target directs local buyers to local suppliers, which permanently shrinks the market foreign vendors can serve.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to domestic memory output, which caps how many local chips can be built.
entries.statement: China has set a national target of 9,800 exaflops of computing capacity by 2030 backed by $532 billion, with 76 percent of its chip demand to be met by domestic suppliers.
entries.title: China sets a state target to serve most of its own chip demand

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No further compute contract delay notice or site-financing shortfall is reported for 2 consecutive quarters.
entries.mechanism: Contracts are signed years before the buildings exist, so buyers protect themselves with clauses that let them delay payment when a site is late.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to permitting and power connection timelines at named campuses.
entries.statement: Buyers of compute capacity are now writing and using delay clauses because the sites behind their contracts are slipping.
entries.title: Compute contracts start carrying delay and default clauses

entries.falsifiableTrigger: No buyer reports a memory pre-buy in its capital plan for 2 consecutive quarters, or memory contract prices fall.
entries.mechanism: When parts are scarcer than money, buying early is cheaper than waiting, so buyers hold memory on their own balance sheets.
entries.sensitivity: Most sensitive to memory prices turning, which would leave pre-bought stock overpriced.
entries.statement: Cloud buyers are now adding money to their own capital budgets purely to buy memory ahead of need.
entries.title: Buyers pre-buy memory into their own capital budgets
